blocks.text: Risk management specialists often struggle with the differences between Windows and Mac versions of Word. The primary change you need to remember is the Command ⌘ key. On Windows, you use the Control key for most shortcuts. On your Mac, swap that for the Command ⌘ key. For example, saving is ⌘ + S instead of Ctrl + S. Copying is ⌘ + C, and pasting is ⌘ + V. If you find your formatting shifts when you move files between Windows and Mac, check your paragraph styles and font settings first.
Essential Word shortcuts for your daily workflow

Efficiency in Word comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Use these shortcuts to move through your risk registers without reaching for the trackpad. To move by word, hold Option ⌥ and press the Left or Right arrow keys. To jump to the start or end of a line, hold Command ⌘ and press the Left or Right arrow keys. If you need to select text, hold Shift ⇧ while using those same movement keys. This simple practice saves you minutes every hour during long drafting sessions.

blocks.text: If Word crashes or freezes, do not panic. Force quit by pressing ⌘ + Option ⌥ + Esc. Then, check for updates in the Microsoft AutoUpdate app. If the problem persists, run First Aid in your Mac Disk Utility to verify your disk permissions.

blocks.text: Why risk managers use Lazur on Mac

Lazur acts as a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It helps you get work done in Word without clicking through nested menus. When you need to find a specific setting, hold Option ⌥ + Command ⌘ and ask. Lazur circles the button or menu item you are looking for. This is useful when you are deep in a report and cannot remember where a specific tool is hidden.

Dictation is a powerful way to get your thoughts into a document quickly. Hold the fn key to start dictating. Lazur provides clean, formatted text at your cursor in Word. This works well for drafting initial risk descriptions or capturing meeting notes while you are looking at your screen. It is included in your usage and helps you avoid the fatigue of typing every single word of a long assessment.

Consistency is the foundation of good risk management. Use templates to ensure every risk report follows the same structure. Learn how to [create a template in word](/how-to/create-a-template-in-word) so you never start from a blank page. If you include many references, learn how to [insert a citation in word](/how-to/insert-a-citation-in-word) to manage your sources properly. These habits reduce the time you spend on formatting and let you focus on the actual risk analysis.

faq.question: Can I use Word macros on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but they may behave differently than on Windows. Some advanced VBA functions are not available on the Mac version. Always test your macros in a copy of your document first.

faq.question: Why is Word slow on my Mac?
faq.answer: Slow performance often comes from large documents with many images or complex tables. Try saving your document as a new file, or disable auto-save if you are working on a massive file, though remember to save manually with ⌘ + S.

faq.question: How do I move from Word to other risk platforms?
faq.answer: Most GRC platforms allow you to import Word or Excel files. Export your data as a CSV or XML file to ensure the cleanest import into your risk management software.
